reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is cryptocurrency news and commentary about Stellar, Ripple, stablecoins, financial regulation, and market developments. Historical Apple and Amazon returns accompany the speaker's personal XRP view, but the available video evidence describes no guaranteed XRP return or direct instruction to buy, and notes promotional links and investment risks. The 20% stablecoin example is presented as a reported IMF statement, regulation is discussed, and an unrelated Ripple claim is qualified as uncertain rather than presented as the speaker's own offer.

opening.argument: Judge, the return examples do more than provide background. The speaker says, “these are the kind of gains and aggregate returns that i'm here for,” then identifies XRP as one of his own investments. The description gives viewers a link to open a custody account. Taken together, that is a pathway from extraordinary appreciation examples to a means of participating in crypto. The speaker does not explicitly promise that XRP will repeat those returns, but the sequence encourages viewers to consider it through that lens.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the Amazon figure is historical, but that does not explain why the speaker immediately relates those gains to the investments he seeks, including XRP. Nor does the absence of a guaranteed return settle whether the account link turns the discussion into a solicitation. The FTX item shows that news is present; it does not make the investment framing disappear.

The speaker expressly describes XRP as an investment “for myself,” while the description warns viewers not to invest based on the videos and says they could lose their entire investment. A possible route to an account does not establish a deceptive token-purchase offer.

He also says “real wealth is made in times like this” and promotes a deal he says will close. The closing deadline concerns the paid group, not a token sale; nonetheless, it puts urgency beside an appreciation narrative and investment-related promotions. That combination warrants more scrutiny than treating each statement as isolated commentary.

opening.argument: The news format also serves a promotional function. The speaker moves from market developments to his conviction that XRP could become part of the digital-asset framework, then closes by directing viewers to the links and urging them to join the paid group. The description supplies an account-opening link and identifies its links as affiliate or paid promotions. A judge should assess the full viewer journey, not only the factual news segments: commentary about XRP appreciation sits alongside invitations to enter the speaker's commercial ecosystem.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites a genuine FTX news item and genuine group features. Neither rules out promotion as another purpose of the video. The speaker explicitly asks viewers to check the description links and sign up for the group, while the description discloses affiliate or paid promotions. The issue is not whether news appears, but whether the investment commentary helps steer viewers toward those offers.

The speaker also discusses risks, including a purported 20% stablecoin return that he characterizes as a pyramid, and qualifies the Ripple central-bank claim as something he cannot independently verify.
